source_excerpts.text:
I have not resolved the unrestricted near-quadratic statement. I have neither a deterministic algorithm satisfying your bound for every fixed $\delta>0$, nor a lower bound excluding all such algorithms.

The strongest results obtained are:


- A complete conditional bit compiler: sufficiently low-rank rational identities give your exact integer algorithm, including computable preprocessing, denominator handling, intermediate precision, indexing and memory costs. In particular, $\omega_{\mathbb Q}=2$ would suffice without a separately supplied identity oracle.
- An explicit rational degeneration from the proposed ternary kernel filtration, with its boundary term and interpolation costs retained.
- A general obstruction to the direct homogeneous-product/full-dual packing route. Within the supplied two-round criterion, ternary forms cannot certify an exponent below $5/2$. This obstruction also survives two natural enlargements: adding fixed vector-dot fibers and replacing scalar multiplication by the kernel’s alternating pairing.

These are scoped results, not a negative resolution of the full question. The proofs and resource accounting are preserved in    Matrix_Multiplication_Bit_Question_20261108.txt <https://chatgpt.com/library?file_id=libfile_74aea1f9398c8191a2afe21419453ab1&account_id=personal>.


1. What the accepted construction already supplies

I retain OpenAI’s complex-field $9/4$ construction and Pass’s constructive rational successor. The latter supplies computable finite identities and an exact integer implementation with
$O_\gamma\!\left(
n^{9/4+\gamma}M(b+\log n)
\right)$
bit cost for every fixed $\gamma>0$. Its general product/dual criterion has threshold
$\tau>
\frac{3\kappa\log\rho}{2\log(m/q)}.
\tag{1}$
Thus the requested bound is already supplied for $\delta>1/4$. This does not establish every $0<\delta\le 1/4$, including the exact $9/4$ endpoint. arxiv.org <https://arxiv.org/html/2610.28627v2?utm_source=chatgpt.com>

Theorem 5.4 of Amanov–van den Berg–Zuiddam rules out improvements below $9/4$ from its stated degeneration ingredients and composition rules. The theorem concerns a formal operational preorder; it is not a lower bound for arbitrary tensor degenerations, much less arbitrary bit algorithms. The paper explicitly distinguishes those scopes. arxiv.org <https://arxiv.org/html/2610.30054v1?utm_source=chatgpt.com>
